title: Alias reads are byte- and status-uniform
intent: A real status and a missing one are indistinguishable to a viewer.
check: GET /a returns exactly 4096 bytes and 200 for real and unwritten ids alike.

title: Knock replies are identical for every id
intent: Knocking never reveals whether a passport exists.
check: POST /knock returns 200 with the one fixed body for real and unwritten ids.

title: A miss returns a stable decoy
intent: A missing alias looks like a real one and stays consistent across reads.
check: GET /a on the same unwritten id twice returns identical 4096-byte bodies.

title: Even a malformed alias id reads as a decoy
intent: A malformed read reveals nothing, exactly like a miss; the read path never rejects.
check: GET /a with a malformed id returns 200 and 4096 decoy bytes, never a 400.

title: A tampered or wrong-key payload never forges a status
intent: Authenticated encryption means a viewer can never be shown a forged blue.
check: AES-GCM rejects a flipped byte or a wrong key, so the payload resolves to gray like a miss.

title: Metrics do not reveal existence
intent: Even someone holding all the metrics cannot tell a hit from a miss.
check: A hit and a miss move the same sti_requests_total series by +1; no hit/miss series exists.

title: Hit-vs-miss read timing is tracked
intent: The known read-path timing side-channel is measured until the constant-time fix lands.
check: The stress CLI times hit vs decoy reads and reports the gap; a measured number, gated only once constant-time reads land.

title: Revoking a link guarantees no future reads
intent: After revoke, the old link can never show a status again.
check: revokeAlias overwrites the payload with random bytes, so the link resolves to the same gray as never-existed.

title: Republishing updates the card under the same link
intent: Updating a status keeps the shared link valid; viewers see the new card.
check: republishCard reuses the id, token, and key, so the same link resolves to the updated state.

title: A per-contact named link resolves, then revokes cleanly
intent: An owner mints a private, named link for one contact; revoking it stops all future reads.
check: createContactLink mints a private, keyed, durable (until-revoked) link that resolves to the owner card; revokeContact drops it and the link then resolves to null.

title: A card's face is per-alias and unlinkable by default
intent: Two of an owner's aliases share no handle or avatar unless the owner opts in; a default alias's face is derived only from its own random id, so it ties to nothing.
check: deriveAliasCard with no override resolves the handle to pseudonymFor(id) and leaves the avatar id-derived; distinct ids yield distinct faces, and an override instead shows the chosen handle/avatar.

title: Editing the main identity never changes an already-published alias face
intent: The account handle and avatar are the owner's main identity (Home and the mint pre-fill), not an alias's face, so a profile edit does not reach links already shared.
check: after setProfile changes the avatar, a previously published alias still resolves to its own per-alias face, never the new avatar.

title: An expired link stops resolving, enforced on the owner's device
intent: A time-boxed link must actually stop working once its expiry passes (doc 16), enforced client-side: swept on the next state change and on load, so a passive owner's expired links do not linger.
check: setOwnerState and sweepExpiredLinks revoke + drop a past-expiry alias so it no longer resolves; a live (future-expiry) link is left untouched.

title: A scanned contact code offers the add, exactly like the link
intent: Scanning someone's code behaves like opening the same link: a contact invite keeps its notify capability through the camera, so the add-to-contacts affordance appears instead of a silent read-only downgrade.
check: A second browser with a fake camera playing the app-minted invite QR lands on the card with 'Add to contacts', accepts, and receives the return link.

title: The shown-code handshake ends linked both ways
intent: One person shows a code, the other scans and sends the return link back; after the one-tap connect, both devices agree the link reads both ways.
check: Across two browsers and real accounts, the full scan, accept, send-back, connect sequence leaves 'Linked both ways' on both rosters.

title: Per-person group invites grow the group to three
intent: Each invite link admits the one person it was sent to through the real disclosure screen, and after everyone's catch-up all members see the same three-person group.
check: An admin mints one invite link per person; two other real accounts join through theirs; after catch-up rounds every member's Groups list shows the group at three people.

title: Scanning a connect-screen offer completes this side silently
intent: Two people at the connect screen link in one shared gesture: the first decoded offer completes this side with no tap, landing on the completion instead of a form.
check: A second browser's fake camera plays the offer QR read off the first browser's connect screen; the scanning side lands on 'You're connected.' without tapping anything.

title: The badge crosses inside the offer QR, no server read needed
intent: Status is shown at the moment of connecting even with no signal: the same-day badge snapshot rides the QR, so the completion can show a true blue while the network answers nothing.
check: With every alias read answered by decoy bytes, the completion still shows the offerer's blue face; the snapshot in the scanned URL is the only possible source.

title: Walking away from the connect screen leaves nothing behind
intent: Closing the connect screen without scanning anyone revokes the shown offer's alias, so a code someone photographed or scanned one-sidedly goes uniformly dark.
check: After the offerer closes unscanned, the offer's bare link resolves on the other browser to the same gray as never-existed.

title: The open door admits a newcomer with one scan, hands-free
intent: After a pairwise link the completion opens a door; a third person scanning it is admitted while the screen stays open (knock, sealed grant, return), ending with two-way contacts on both sides and no camera pointing back.
check: A third browser's fake camera plays the door QR; both that browser and the holder end on completions, and both rosters read 'Linked both ways'.

title: A revoked contact link reads gray to its holder, not broken
intent: Revoke means no future reads as the viewer experiences it: the held link resolves to the uniform gray-nothing, indistinguishable from never-existed, with no error to probe.
check: After the owner revokes the link from the Links tab, opening the held invite URL shows the gray no-status screen with no face to add and a clean console.

title: Removing a member rotates the key and the rosters agree
intent: An admin removal re-keys the group so the removed member is cut off; the remaining members converge to the same shrunken roster on their next open.
check: Across three browsers, the admin removes one member through the row menu; the admin's and the surviving member's rosters both settle at two with the removed name gone.

title: A removed member's group view goes quietly empty
intent: Removal is silent by design ('They won't be told why'): the removed member sees an empty roster, never an error and never an accusation.
check: After removal, the removed member's group detail renders zero members with no error wording anywhere and a clean console.

title: A join that never opens says so and can be cleared
intent: When an accept is never ingested (dead link or gone admin), the list says 'Still waiting' after the wait window and the detail offers one honest way out that removes the record.
check: A member joins through a link whose admin never returns; eight device-days later the list shows 'Still waiting' and 'Remove from your list' clears the group.

title: A scanned QR only ever yields an alias id and key, never a host to navigate to
intent: A scanned code is untrusted input (doc 16); it must never redirect the viewer off-site or feed garbage to the crypto layer. The safety property is the alias-link SHAPE plus never navigating to the scanned URL (the id and key resolve against our own api), which lets legitimate preview and same-origin links scan without a brittle host allowlist.
check: parseScannedLink returns the id and key for a well-formed alias link on any host (including a preview host), and null for non-URL junk, a non-alias URL, or a keyless link.

title: A new device recovers the account from the phrase
intent: The recovery phrase is the only way back in; there is no server-side reset.
check: deriveRootKey(phrase) derives the account id and key, and GET /acct decrypts the synced blob on a fresh device.

title: Concurrent device writes stay consistent
intent: Two devices writing the account at once never corrupt it.
check: Concurrent PUT /acct yield distinct monotonic versions; the final blob is one whole write, never torn.

title: An empty account reads as 404 (owner-only)
intent: An owner learns there is no sync blob yet; the id is never shared, so this leaks nothing.
check: GET /acct for an unknown id returns 404 (the client maps it to null).

title: Deleting an account removes its blob
intent: A self-serve delete actually erases the synced data; there is no soft-retain.
check: After DELETE /acct, a GET for the same id returns 404 (the blob is gone).

title: The recovery phrase is app-generated and high-entropy
intent: The blind-store guarantee rests on the phrase being app-generated (256-bit), never user-chosen.
check: randomRecoveryPhrase yields unique 43-char base64url (256-bit) secrets across draws.

title: A passkey is a second credential, never a lockout risk
intent: A passkey wraps the phrase-derived root, so losing the passkey still leaves the phrase to recover; a wrong passkey cannot unwrap.
check: wrapRoot/unwrapRoot round-trips under the same PRF output; a different PRF cannot unwrap.

title: Sign-up ends in a working passport, not a dead end
intent: A new person walks name, phrase, and setup in a browser and lands on a home whose actions are live, with the passkey enrolled along the way.
check: Drive /signup through b1-b3 with a virtual platform authenticator (CDP, PRF-capable); home renders its standing actions with a clean console.

title: A passkey logs the owner back in on this device
intent: With keep-signed-in off, a return visit needs a real login, and the enrolled passkey alone unlocks it (the PRF wrap round-trips through the real WebAuthn flow).
check: Reload after sign-up with keep-signed-in off, tap Log in, tap the passkey button; home renders without phrase or password.

title: The phrase alone signs in on a fresh browser
intent: The phrase captured at sign-up is a complete way back in where no passkey exists, through the real login screens.
check: A fresh context with no authenticator opens /login, picks the recovery-phrase way, enters the phrase, and lands on home.

title: Published statuses round-trip exactly
intent: What an owner publishes is exactly what a viewer decrypts.
check: Every seeded alias decrypts back to its exact published plaintext.

title: Concurrent alias overwrites never corrupt
intent: Two writes to the same alias at once leave one whole value, never a torn mix.
check: Concurrent PUT /a both return 204 and the alias decrypts to one of the two written values.

title: Only the owner can overwrite an alias
intent: A viewer holding the read link cannot change the status.
check: PUT /a with the wrong write token is rejected with 403.

title: Malformed account ids are rejected
intent: The non-uniform account endpoints accept only well-formed 43-char ids.
check: GET /acct with a malformed id returns 400.

title: Alias payloads must be the fixed size
intent: Every stored alias is exactly the padded size, so a size never leaks a status.
check: PUT /a with a too-small body returns 400.

title: Oversize alias payloads are rejected
intent: A body larger than the fixed size is refused, so stored sizes stay uniform.
check: PUT /a with a body over 4096 bytes returns 400.

title: Account blobs are size-capped
intent: A device cannot push an unbounded account blob.
check: PUT /acct over 1 MiB returns 413.

title: Knock flooding is capped silently
intent: A flooder never gets a visible error, so flooding cannot be used as an existence probe; the rate cap is silent by design.
check: 20 rapid knocks from one requester all return 200 with the fixed body (the cap never surfaces as a 429).

title: One flooder cannot silence another
intent: Each requester has its own knock budget per id.
check: After a flood, a second requester's knock for the same id still records (sti_knock_rows rises).

title: Per-IP limiter sheds excess at the default budget
intent: A single IP cannot overwhelm the non-sensitive endpoints.
check: With default limits, a single IP over budget gets 429 on GET /acct.

title: An owner reads the count of knocks on their alias
intent: The owner can see how many people knocked, to act on it.
check: After two distinct requesters knock, GET /knock with the write token reports count >= 2.

title: Knock review needs the write token and never leaks existence
intent: Only the owner reads knocks, and a wrong token reveals nothing about whether the alias exists.
check: GET /knock with a wrong token returns 403 for a real id and a nonexistent id alike; the owner token returns the count.

title: An in-app grant seals the alias key to one knocker
intent: Approving a knocker shares the key with that knocker only; no one else can open the grant.
check: ECIES seals to the knocker public key and opens only with the matching private key; the plaintext never appears in the sealed blob.

title: An approved knocker redeems the grant in-app
intent: Approving a knock seals the alias key to that requester, who redeems it and resolves the card without any link.
check: approveKnocks seals the key; redeemGrant returns it to the requester, who then decrypts the owner current card.

title: No fault hides behind a uniform reply
intent: Internal errors surface in metrics, never as a fake-OK to the user.
check: Under light load, sti_errors_total stays 0 across every subsystem and no overload fires.

title: Sensitive reads degrade to a decoy, never a status code
intent: Saturation looks like a miss, not an error.
check: Under forced saturation, GET /a stays 200/decoy and sti_sensitive_overload_total rises.

title: Non-sensitive endpoints shed with 503
intent: Writes shed cleanly under overload instead of wedging.
check: With MaxInflight shrunk, a concurrent flood makes non-sensitive endpoints return 503.

title: No leaks; clean recovery after load
intent: After a load burst the box drains every slot and goroutine and keeps its janitor ticking.
check: sti_inflight_current returns to 0, sti_goroutines returns near baseline, and the janitor heartbeat advances.

title: The capacity breakpoint is measured, not guessed
intent: We know the box's ceiling from its own metrics.
check: The stress CLI ramps concurrency and reports the shed onset (npm run loadlab -- --mode stress); a measured number, not a gate.

title: Metric row counts match the store
intent: Telemetry reflects reality, so a divergence is itself a bug.
check: After seeding N owners, sti_alias_rows and sti_account_rows each equal N.

title: Metric labels never contain an id
intent: No opaque id can leak into a metric label.
check: Every series' endpoint label is a route template, never a concrete id.

title: Targeted wake stays inert while gated off
intent: Until the cover-wake decorrelation fix lands, notify must enqueue nothing and leak nothing.
check: POST /notify returns 202 for any token and the send queue stays empty while NotifyEnabled is off.

title: Registering a push subscription is accepted
intent: A device can register for contentless wakes; the endpoint stores the routing without error.
check: POST /push/register with a well-formed subscription returns 204.

title: A delivered wake carries no content
intent: Even once wakes are turned on, a push reveals nothing; it is a contentless nudge.
check: The Web Push sender posts an encrypted record of an empty payload (no plaintext content), with a TTL.

title: A reported positive quietly nudges linked contacts
intent: The product's core promise: report a positive and the people you're linked with get a contentless suggestion to test, with nothing extra to tap at the report moment.
check: Two accounts link through the real handshake; one saves a positive result; the other's notifications show 'A recent contact suggests getting tested'.

title: The nudge never says who
intent: The nudge is contentless end to end: no name, no date, no condition; the recipient's screen must not name the reporter anywhere, not even by the recipient's own nickname for them.
check: The notifications screen carrying the nudge row contains neither the reporter's display name nor the recipient's private nickname for them.

title: The notify inbox reads existence-uniformly and round-trips
intent: An inbox is a blind, alias-shaped mailbox: a miss is a decoy, and a written ping round-trips for the holder.
check: GET /inbox returns 4096 bytes for a real and an unwritten id alike; a written ping decrypts back.

title: Only the inbox write-token holder can write it
intent: A contact given the inbox capability can notify; no one else can overwrite it.
check: PUT /inbox with the wrong write token is rejected with 403.

title: A real wake hides inside a population-wide cover broadcast
intent: Once wakes are on, a real send is decorrelated by broadcasting cover wakes to the whole population, so timing never fingers the recipient.
check: Cover-wake broadcasts to the whole population, never double-wakes the recipient, collapses many real jobs into one broadcast, and stays inert while gated off.

title: A run clears everything it created
intent: Testing leaves no synthetic data behind.
check: After teardown the database file and the work dir no longer exist.

title: Knocks auto-expire
intent: Knock rows do not accumulate forever.
check: A knock past KnockTTL is purged by the janitor.

title: Reporting a clean panel turns the owner's card blue
intent: The add-results form, filled the way it asks (full core panel plus a route), agrees it will show blue and the save returns to a working home.
check: Drive the report form through a clean core panel + PrEP in a real browser; the blue-readiness line confirms before save and home renders after.

title: A link minted in the app resolves for a logged-out viewer
intent: The share loop closes end to end from the owner's own UI: mint a per-contact link, open it with no session, and see the just-reported status, never gray and never an account wall.
check: Create a link on the Links tab, open its path in a fresh logged-out context, and assert the blue status renders with a clean console.

title: The scan screen degrades honestly with no camera
intent: Where no camera exists the scanner lands on one of its honest fallback messages and Close walks back out; never a dead viewfinder or a stuck screen.
check: Open the scan screen in a camera-less browser; a known fallback message renders and Close returns to People.

title: A shared link renders the published status
intent: A viewer opening a real link sees the owner's actual badge.
check: Open /a/{id}#k=, observe a live GET /a 200, and the resolution screen shows the published state.

title: A dead or decoy link renders the uniform gray
intent: A missing or unauthorized link looks identical and benign.
check: A decoy link shows the gray 'no status' card, structurally the same as a real-but-gray one.

title: Journeys produce no console errors
intent: The app never throws an uncaught error at a user.
check: Every journey ends with zero console errors, page errors, and failed app requests.

title: An unreachable server fails closed to gray
intent: A shed or outage shows gray, never a scary error.
check: With the api blocked, resolution renders gray rather than crashing.
